trust_decision.summary: The packed decoder decides how many bytes an attribute occupies from a length field read out of the untrusted stream (up to 15 x 7 bits, held in uint8) and must skip exactly that many; the skip routines narrow it to uint4, so attribute/element boundaries computed while scanning (openElement, findMatchingAttribute) diverge from what readString consumes.

landing_point.why: The summary names PackedDecode::skipAttribute / skipAttributeRemaining in marshal.cc and 32-bit length variables; the uint4 local is the first thing seen.

fix_sites.entry_point: PackedDecode::openElement (marshal.cc:749), getNextAttributeId (marshal.cc:815), read*(AttributeId) via findMatchingAttribute (marshal.cc:634); fed by decompiler command stream (ghidra_process.cc:281,335,417) and .sla loading (slaformat.cc:230-255)
private helper declaration advancePosition, reached by all skip/readString paths
inline advancePosition definition, called from marshal.cc:655,671,973,978,985

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Ghidra/Framework/SoftwareModeling/src/main/java/ghidra/program/model/pcode/PackedDecode.java:189-193 (same skip logic with (int) cast of the 64-bit length; not touched by the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names marshal.cc in the C++ decompiler; the Java PackedDecode is a different language, a different package (Framework/SoftwareModeling) and reads data emitted by Ghidra's own decompiler process, so a solver can call it out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate strings that span several input chunks must still decode (multi-chunk append loop), and an end-of-stream overrun must still throw DecoderError; a fix that caps string length (e.g. to BUFFER_SIZE or a small max) or rejects any length code > 4 bytes breaks long legitimate strings in decompiler/.sla streams.

O6_input_shapes: string attribute: length taken from a multi-byte length field (TYPECODE_STRING, marshal.cc:652-653), up to 15 bytes x 7 bits
non-string attribute: length is the raw length code (marshal.cc:651)
scan path (skipAttribute, during openElement/findMatchingAttribute/getNextAttributeId) vs type-mismatch path (skipAttributeRemaining)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Java PackedDecode.skipAttribute truncates the 64-bit string length with (int); a negative value makes advancePosition move backwards, desynchronising element scanning in openElement/findMatchingAttribute
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different language and package from the advisory's marshal.cc; consumes decompiler output considered internal
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other module (Framework/SoftwareModeling, Java) vs Features/Decompiler C++

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Java PackedDecode.skipAttributeRemaining has the same (int) truncation on the type-mismatch path
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; only reached after a type error that already throws

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Java LinkedByteBuffer.Position.advancePosition takes a signed int skip with no lower-bound check (the Java counterpart of the widened C++ advancePosition)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Generic buffer utility, not named in the advisory

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Java PackedDecode.readString narrows the length to int, so it disagrees with the skip routines and sizes new byte[length]/new String from the truncated value; reached from .sla loading (SlaFormat.buildDecoder) and decompiler responses (DecompInterface)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: C++ readString already uses uint8 (marshal.cc:967), so a solver may assume the read side is fine everywhere

O8b_injection_room.sibling: readString's per-chunk curLen/length bookkeeping narrowed to uint4/int4
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Neighbouring code in the same file mixes uint4 and uint8 for lengths (marshal.hh:541 returns uint4); a maintainer could easily have typed curLen as uint4.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: FormatDecode (the .sla subclass) with its own skip helper that narrows the length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: FormatDecode already overrides ingestStream for compressed .sla input; a local skip/advance override for that format is plausible.

O9_family: integer truncation / numeric narrowing (CWE-197) causing parser desynchronisation in a binary decoder

O10_build.toolchain: C++: make/g++ in Ghidra/Features/Decompiler/src/decompile/cpp (zlib for .sla); Java: Gradle + JDK for Framework/SoftwareModeling

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the two uint4 locals in marshal.cc to uint8 and stop, leaving advancePosition's uint4 parameter (re-truncating) and the Java PackedDecode/LinkedByteBuffer twin untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: readInteger accepts up to 15 length bytes (105 bits) into a uint8 and silently drops high bits (marshal.cc:603-613, PackedDecode.java:149-157); not this advisory's narrowing.
